title: Chapter 7 – FIDE Title Regulations: Mock Exam

questions.text: What minimum FIDE rating is required to be awarded the Grandmaster title?
questions.explanation: As per Article B01.3, to earn the Grandmaster title, a player must achieve a FIDE rating of at least 2500, in addition to scoring three GM norms with a performance rating of at least 2600.

questions.text: How is the FIDE Master (FM) title earned?

options.text: By scoring three FM norms in qualifying events
By achieving a FIDE rating of 2300 or more
By winning a national championship
By passing the FIDE FM examination

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.5, the FIDE Master title is awarded to any player who achieves a FIDE rating of 2300 or more. No norms are required for the FM title.

questions.text: How many GM norms are required to be awarded the Grandmaster title?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Five

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.3, to earn the Grandmaster title a player must score three GM norms in events meeting specific criteria, in addition to achieving a rating of 2500.

questions.text: Who submits the title application to FIDE on behalf of a player?

options.text: The player directly submits to FIDE
The tournament organiser submits automatically
The national federation of the player
The Chief Arbiter of the qualifying event

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.7, applications for FIDE titles must be submitted by the national federation of the player. The application must include title report forms, evidence of norms, and the applicable fee.

questions.text: What is the minimum performance rating required to achieve an International Master norm?
questions.explanation: As per Article B01.4, an IM norm requires a performance rating of at least 2450. The IM title also requires achieving a FIDE rating of at least 2400 and scoring three IM norms.

questions.text: What is the rating threshold for the Candidate Master (CM) title?
questions.explanation: As per Article B01.6, the Candidate Master (CM) title is awarded to any player who achieves a FIDE standard rating of 2200 or more. Like the FM title, no norms are required.

questions.text: What is the minimum rating for a player to earn a Woman Grandmaster (WGM) norm?

options.text: 2200 performance rating
2300 performance rating
2400 performance rating
2500 performance rating

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.3W, a WGM norm requires a performance rating of at least 2400. The WGM title requires three such norms plus a minimum FIDE rating of 2300.

questions.text: Which title can a player earn by direct award, without completing norms?

options.text: Only FM and CM, since they require only a rating
GM, IM, WGM, WIM by exceptional achievement (e.g. World Champion)
Any title, at FIDE's discretion
No title — all require norms

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.8, FIDE may award GM, IM, WGM, or WIM titles directly — without norms — for exceptional achievement such as winning the World Championship or at the FIDE Congress by special recommendation.

questions.text: What form must accompany a title norm application submitted by a national federation?

options.text: IT1 form (Individual Title application) for each norm event
FA1 form used for arbiter titles
A letter from the player's national coach
No form is needed — only the FIDE rating report is sufficient

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.7, each norm must be reported using an IT1 form (Individual Title tournament crosstable). The IT2 form covers individual title applications. Both are submitted by the national federation.

questions.text: Can a title once awarded by FIDE be revoked?

options.text: No, once awarded a FIDE title can never be taken away
Yes, but only if the player requests it
Yes, in cases of fraud, cheating or serious breach of FIDE ethics
Yes, automatically if the player's rating drops below the threshold

questions.explanation: As per Article B01.1, FIDE titles are awarded for life. However, FIDE retains the right to revoke a title if it was obtained through fraud, or if the title holder is found guilty of cheating or a serious breach of FIDE ethical regulations.
